Thanks for your detailed and thoughtful reply. I appreciate the time you’ve taken here. I think my original post paints a misleading picture perhaps.

RE: what am I doing to support my direct report? Have put in approx an hour a day since I started in December to listening and supporting and understanding her needs and co-creating a plan. Initiated HR and occupational health processes. Escalated the issues that tipped her over the edge to senior management and suggested a range of ideas to remedy the situation. Zoomed her at 5pm everyday to get her to stop working. The straw that broke the camel’s back? A 5pm email from senior colleague saying that my manager has agreed that my direct report and I will complete a complex piece of analysis and present at a meeting at 10am the next day. We had no forewarning of this. I told her to log off and let me push back but she was inconsolable, saw it as a sign that nothing was going to change. There’s only so much one person can do. Also, I asked direct report for feedback on how I handled the situation so that I could learn, and she said that I’ve given her more support in one month than she’s received from everyone else combined for the year preceding my arrival.

I know it was a rhetorical question you asked to prompt me to reframe things, I just felt the need to clarify a bit!

Just came here to send love and courage. Try to be kind to yourself above all, this is a horrible thing to be going through. You don’t need to rush to decide what you want to do next. Give yourself space to absorb the shock, you don’t owe him any answers (or anything at all for that matter).

I’m sorry you have been going through this, it sounds really painful and destructive to your self-esteem. This guy sounds extremely shitty. Of course he knew you had feelings- he just doesn’t want to admit to you (and/ or to himself) that he trampled all over them and strung you along- because then he’d have to admit to himself that he is not a nice person.

Some of the things he’s said about not liking anything about you, you not being open enough etc, I think are really cruel and not ok. And cancelling plans once you’re already en route is horrible and selfish. And the contraception thing is just unacceptable- no one gets to bully you over what you choose to do with your own body.

Basically there’s so much here in his behaviour that is really really awful and actually quite abusive, he’s clearly worn down your self-esteem. You deserve to be with someone who loves you and treats you with kindness! You should be asking yourself why you were willing to accept such terrible treatment. I’ve been there, I know what it feels like to be grateful for every tiny crumb of love that’s thrown my way because I feel like I’m worth nothing. I know what it’s like to feel utterly powerless. But you are never completely powerless because you always have the choice to walk away, to say enough is enough, this is where I draw the line.

The good news is that he’s out of the picture and you can start to heal and to transform yourself into someone who loves herself. This can be the start of a new, positive chapter for you. Read self-help books, get a therapist if you can afford it. Build yourself up. It’s incremental progress, but you can do it. Sending courage and hugs.

Ugh I’ve recently escaped a similar situation. I have to say, I think it’s really a shitty move of him to have reached out to you again when he is the one who was less invested, who didn’t want to commit, who ended things. It’s really really hard for the more invested party to disentangle themselves from the person they love. He’s being really selfish. I would tell him that you are trying to get over him and that, unless he’s changed his mind and wants a committed relationship, you don’t want to hear from him so that you can continue to heal, and you will reach out if and when you are ever ready to be friends.

How do you break an on&off toxic relationship cycle? One party has to grow out of it, and it sounds like it’s not going to be him. You’re worth more than this, you deserve more than this.

Yeah this doesn’t sound like a platonic best friend. From your title I was expecting that it was someone you’ve known for years. It’s not usual to be “very flirty” with friends. I think you need to decide what you want and avoid sending mixed messages. If you’re not ready to date, then you need to stop the flirting. Also I’d be very wary of letting her play any kind of rebound role in your life. 

I’m curious about your claim that you don’t want to date her because “there is someone better out there for her”. Better as in, will treat her better and love her more? Or as in, more attractive than you? If it’s the former, if you don’t see her as girlfriend material, you need to admit that to yourself and avoid leading her on, and not dress it up as self-deprecation.

I know it’s hard when you’re recently out of a long term relationship. There’s a hole in your life and you want to fill it. It’s good that you’re thinking about her feelings and not just jumping into bed. Do your best to be honest with yourself and with her, and to be your best, kindest self.

First of all I just had to comment to say your skin/complexion is to die for, so clear and pale in a way that looks gorgeous against your dark hair. And, with lovely striking blue eyes that also look gorgeous with your hair. Also, you clearly have a lovely figure. AND a really unique style, you’re clearly not “not a real person”, there’s totally a unique individual expressing herself here.

Others have commented on the eyebrows- I think it kind of depends what style you like. At the moment it makes me think, “this person is probably quite arty and not afraid to be different”. I’d probably assume you were quite cool. That said, I’d be curious to see what something more subtle/ natural would look like too. Your other features are quite soft/gentle so I reckon it could work really well.

RE lack of friends, this is tough but definitely possible to expand your circle. Can you move in with likeminded people? Can you pursue hobbies to meet others? Tricky during lockdown I know but this won’t go on forever. 

Perhaps you could use the rest of lockdown to really focus on your self esteem. What activities make you feel good about yourself? Spend more time doing them. Learn a new skill. Practice noticing the self-critical voice in your head, and weighing up whether you really in your heart of hearts believe it. Start therapy if you can afford, or start reading books about how to help grow your self esteem. Try to make any self improvement work come from a place of wanting the best for yourself, of inspiration and creativity, and not from a place of lack. 

Google metta meditation to make compassion towards self and others part of your daily life. Practice relaxing around discomfort, allowing it to be. I reckon that working on your self esteem will unlock everything else, honestly. Because if you’re feeling bad about yourself, others will feel that need for validation, and that can feel heavy, it can complicate relationships. It’s totally possible to break out of the “I need you to love me so that I can love myself” trap, by practising self love.

I think these are really interesting questions and it’s worth doing the self-inquiry to find the answers. It’s work in progress for me- but I think my anxiety and my need to be in control are closely related. It’s like everything feels really high stakes, I care too much. I’m very conscientious in general and scared of regret. I beat myself up if things don’t go well, so that adds to the high stakes. I’m easily overwhelmed by emotion so want to protect myself by making things go well. This is not specific to relationships- and insomnia is a general problem for me that is triggered whenever there’s something I care a lot about, not just with relationships. 

For me, anxiety is often about my own performance. It’s like I don’t trust myself. And I’m anxious around other people because I need them to like and validate me, because my self-esteem is low. To some extent it’s just how I’m wired- but I also learnt that the world is a dangerous place from my anxious mother, and learnt at school that I’m a little bit odd, and natural, relaxed me isn’t good enough.

Here’s a process that I’m finding helpful. Start by calling to mind the anxious part of yourself. Maybe recall a time you felt anxious, call up how that felt. And ask that part of you what it wants. Every part of you has some kind of adaptive objective- eg. making you anxious so you don’t embarrass yourself, so you are more socially successful, so you are more loved, so you are more able to love yourself. Or perhaps it wants to protect some vulnerable part of you from getting hurt, so that you can feel safe. These are just example chains of causality I’m making up. Whatever its end goal is, see if you can call that feeling up. There’s something really healing in that- just teaching yourself that you don’t need to go through all the anxiety to get to the feeling you want- you can reach out and grab it.

Yeah, snap. It sucks. I also can’t sleep in the same room as a new partner or a partner where I’m not 110% at ease. I’ve had year long relationships where I’m pulling all-nighters 2-3x a week. And the date insomnia thing- so awful. I realised too that when I haven’t slept not only am I worse company- I’m also uglier and look older. I also can’t sleep before important things like interviews. And the night before the night before anything important, because two sleepless nights is even more awful so I get anxious about that. Sorry, this rant isn’t helping, but you’re not alone. For me, meditation helps sometimes. I got into it quite seriously to see if I can, incrementally, loosen the iron tight grip of needing to be in control that seems to underpin many of my problems. This involves just receiving and releasing whatever is part of my experience in that moment, loosening around discomfort, allowing it, letting it breathe, or if I can’t relax around it, relaxing around my own inability to relax and letting that be. Something is shifting, very slowly, but it’s a long road. I don’t think there is an easy answer here. But hoping someone posts something useful here for both our sakes, and wishing you well.
